utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody in the courtroom. The witness should be brought in, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Skrbic. Welcome back to the courtroom. I have to remind you that the affirmation to tell the truth you made at the beginning of your testimony still applies. Mr. Tolimir is continuing his examination. Mr. Tolimir, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. May the Lord bring peace to this courtroom, and may the outcome of this trial be decided by providence and not in accordance with my wishes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday, we were dealing with document 65 ter 0014.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see 65 ter 0014. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, please tell us what sort of document this is. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document from the Secretariat of the Defence Ministry in Zvornik, and it concerns an order that relates to the mobilisation of buses. It's an order for other departments and secretariats. It has been signed by -- Your Honours, I do apologise. I have to rephrase my answer. You can't see the memorandum above the number 0221. It should say "The Memorandum of the Ministry of Defence of the Republika Srpska," because given the signature, I've recognised the person who signed the document. It was compiled in the Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska and forwarded to the Secretariat of the Defence Ministry in Zvornik. The contents of the document are quite obvious. In the document itself it concerns the mobilisation of buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. I'll read out what it says here: "Pursuant to a request by the Main Staff of the Republika Srpska Army ... immediately mobilise buses." "All available buses," I forgot to mention that. My question is as follows: Does this document correctly characterise the request of the Main Staff as a request? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this concept is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: What is the nature of this document and what's the difference between the concept of a request, the concept of a proposal, and the concept of an order? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A request from the Main Staff, the request from the Main Staff that we discussed yesterday was a matter of announcing the needs of the VRS for buses, but this document from the ministry of Republika Srpska, forwarded to the Zvornik Secretariat is of an imperative kind. It, in fact, represents an order according to which it is necessary to mobilise buses, that is stated categorically.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. Did those who receive the document have the obligation to act according to what the document stated? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were obliged to take action in accordance with the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Was that a result of the request or, as you said, these documents here -- or, rather, these orders from the Ministry of Defence? What was the basis for this obligation? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Ministry of Defence of the Secretariat in Zvornik explained its orders from the Main Staff and issued the order to mobilise buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. In the last sentence it says: "Keep this ministry informed immediately about the actions taken ..." I'll repeat what I said: "Keep the ministry informed about actions taken ..." and do so immediately. So my question is as follows: Can you tell us why this is stated in the document, and whom do they have to inform, the Main Staff or the ministry? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, allow me to read out the sentence correctly: "Keep this ministry regularly informed about the actions taken in connection with the aforementioned request." The sentence quite clearly shows that the Zvornik Secretariat has the obligation to inform the Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska, not the Main Staff of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this 65 ter 0014 document please be admitted into evidence? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 0014 shall be assigned Exhibit D342. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now see the following document 1D1029 in the e-court system. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We can see this document now, and we can see that it says "Memorandum, Republika Srpska," 12th of July is the date. That's the memorandum you were mentioning, 12th of July, 1995. It's a document from the Ministry of Defence of the Republika Srpska and addressed to the Secretariat of the Ministry of Defence in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I interrupt you for a moment. The English version, the English part we have on the screen doesn't correspond with the B/C/S one. We need the correct translation. I don't know which problem we have. Perhaps there is no translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Possibly the wrong page or document was uploaded into e-court because this one we just saw was from 1994 and didn't relate to the B/C/S one. Mr. Gajic, do you have any explanation for that? Is there an English translation or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is a document from the Prosecution list, so they uploaded the document into the e-court system. In the course of Mr. Tolimir's first or second question, it doesn't require a complete translation. I will try and check to see whether it's possible to locate a full translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, you should proceed without a translation. I hope you will be able, with the assistance of Mr. Gajic, to show us the right page of the translation. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, please tell us, if possible, whose signature can be found on this document and do you recognise it? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the lower right-hand quarter, it says "Assistant minister, Momcilo Kovacevic." It was probably typed out on a computer. This can be quite clearly seen. But D. Kapetina, Dragan Kapetina, I think, signed on his behalf, because it says "for" under assistant minister, and then he signed it. So he had the authority to sign this document in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Skrbic, in the lower left-hand corner, can you see the stamp, the telegram stamp with information about how it was sent, and is there anything that you conclude on the basis of that stamp that might be of interest to the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I can't interpret this stamp because there are some figures that it contains that are confusing me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We do have an English translation of this document which I would like to be put up. It does have information in it that goes to another issue that the witness was asked about. Or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Is that uploaded in e-court? And if so, can you give us the respective number?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Ms. Stewart can put it on Sanction apparently right now. And the issue is also in one paragraph, you could just read it, which says what time the bus -- or what date the buses are expected to be at the Bratunac stadium, which was an issue yesterday. But we can get that on Sanction, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Now we have an English translation of this document. I hope it's the same document. It's a document of the 12th of July, 1995, Secretariat of the Ministry of Defence in Zvornik. Subject: "Request for Mobilisation of Buses." And for the benefit of all participants I read out the first paragraph: "Pursuant to the request of confidential number," and then follows the number 09/31/12-3/154, "of the VRS Main Staff, dated 12th of July, 1995, for the mobilisation of buses, immediately," in capital letters, "mobilise at least 30 buses with drivers from Zvornik, Visegrad, Vlasenica, Milici, and Bratunac Municipalities. "The buses with drivers must report in Bratunac (sports stadium) by 1430 on the 12th of July, 1995, at the latest. "Immediately report to this ministry on activities carried out pursuant to this request. "For Assistant Minister Momcilo Kovacevic." And then there is on the second page a translation of the stamp we saw earlier on the -- in the B/C/S version. Mr. Tolimir, you should continue and try to adhere with the documents we have had one after the other on the screen. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My question was: Can one see from this stamp -- can one see anything and can you draw any conclusions from the last line that we see here, the last line of the translation? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is clear to me that the encryption people have filled out this stamp, but it is really very difficult for me to try to discern particularly those printed portions of the stamp. So it's not legible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted into evidence, 65 ter 1D1029. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Since there is no English translation attached to this original document, it will be marked for identification pending -- I would say not pending translation, but pending attachment of the correct translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 1D1029 shall be assigned Exhibit D343, marked for identification pending provision of correct translation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Can we now have in e-court 65 ter document 2102. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: What we see here is another letter from the ministry of Republika Srpska. You can see that in the letterhead. It's dated 12th July, 1995, and it was signed by the secretary. Can you perchance recognise this signature?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the signature of Stevan Ivanovic who was the secretary. Can I have the whole document back, please, so that I can see the letterhead in the top left corner. Your Honours, this is not the letterhead of the Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska but, rather, the secretariat, most probably the one in Zvornik. And this letter is sent to the sections. And you can see that it says under the Ministry of Defence departments in Zvornik, Milici, Vlasenica, Sekovici, and Bratunac. That is why this letter was signed by the secretary. Although the name of the secretariat that is in the letterhead is not legible. The secretariat is a lower-ranking organisational unit within the ministry. It pertains to specific regions and comprises a number of municipalities where you have departments of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if you look at the upper right-hand corner, there is another stamp there put by the Zvornik department confirming the receipt. Does that signify that the Zvornik department really received it because it was indicated as a recipient and does that indicate that it was forwarded to the other departments mentioned below? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tolimir. This is exactly how it is, as you put it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Under the word "order" it says: "1. Mobilise immediately all buses except articulated ones. "2. Bus drivers with the buses are to report immediately to the sports centre in Bratunac. "3. If necessary, cancel all regular bus services until further notice. "4. Report by telephone every 30 minutes to the Ministry of Defence Secretariat in Zvornik about the actions taken pursuant to this order. "I shall hold department heads and managers of companies from which the buses are to be requisitioned solely responsible for the implementation of this order." And then we have the signature. Now, my question is, can you tell us what kind of document is this? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by the word "order" used here, one can clearly conclude that this is an order issued by the secretariat to its departments. That's what we explained a minute ago. This order stipulates the way of reporting and who the recipient of the reports should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can, please, this document be admitted into evidence? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 2102 shall be assigned Exhibit D344. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now in e-court have document 1D1035. Thank you. We can see the translation as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Please, can you tell us whose signature can you see on this document and whether the dispatch and the receipt of this document has been confirmed by the encryption service? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to draw everyone's attention that something very important has been added in this letter which is "very urgent" that we see in the top right corner. You asked me about the signature. This was not signed by Momcilo Kovacevic but, rather, by an employee of the Ministry of Defence whose name is Banduka because before the words "assistant minister" you can see the word "for."

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can, please, this document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: First, I would like to have the chance to see the content of this document. Can we have the English translation, please, on the screen. The text itself. Sir, Mr. Skrbic, can you tell us who is writing to whom in this letter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in the letterhead you see that it says the Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska. That's the originating institution, and it is addressed to the Secretariat of the Defence -- of the Ministry of Defence in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Do you see any difference between this document and the document we have seen earlier from the Ministry of Defence to the secretariat of the ministry in Zvornik with the subject: "Request to Mobilise Buses." I remember that we have seen a similar one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there is no difference in the contents. And the only difference that I see and that I pointed out is that it says "very urgent," and you can see that it's been translated into English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can you see from the stamp when it was sent to the recipient?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is another difference there. The previous stamp I wasn't able to read because there it said the 12th of June; whereas, here, in the bottom left corner you can see the date the 12th of July. And this stamp put by the teleprinter operator is completely consistent with the dates in the letter itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And the time indication you can see there, what does it tell you? Can it be enlarged, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first line -- I am really trying to read this as much as I can although it's blurred. But logically, I would say that it was received on the 12th of July at 1840 hours, and then you have a signature. The next line is illegible. Then beneath it says: "Processed on the 12th of July," and the signature is identical. And finally it says: "Forwarded on the 12th of July at 1905," and again the same signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The document will be received into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 1D1035 - I repeat, 1D1035 - shall be assigned Exhibit D345. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we please have D342 again on the screen. Is there a second page of this document? No, I take it there is none. Thank you very much. Mr. Skrbic, if you compare this document with the last one we have seen on the screen, what is the difference between two?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, there is no letterhead of the Ministry of Defence. There is no designation "very urgent," the signature is different, and there is no stamp put by the encryption officer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Tolimir, carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have in e-court document 1D1036. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, what we see here is a document produced by the Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska, dated 13th of July, 1995, addressed to the Secretariat of the Ministry of Defence in Bijeljina. And it's another request for mobilisation of buses. Can you tell me who signed this letter? Can you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was signed by the official whose name appears typed up; in other words, the Assistant Minister Momcilo Kovacevic. So he signed the document itself and that's what the signature reads. In Cyrillic it says "M. Kovacevic."

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, my question is this: Does this signature, M. Kovacevic, appear on other documents? Did it appear on the documents that we showed a few minutes ago? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name Momcilo Kovacevic as assistant minister appeared in the body of the document but the signature was different. It was -- in those other documents, the documents were signed by other individuals who were authorised to sign on behalf of Momcilo Kovacevic, and I know this because some of those signatures I recognise because I knew the people personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, can you see here at bottom left an encryption stamp, and is this stamp a bit more legible than it was on the other documents that I showed you a bit earlier? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it, and it is more legible now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 1D1036 shall be assigned Exhibit D346. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. I -- I am going back to D343. This was some minutes ago received and marked for identification. I was told by the Court Officer that this is now -- the translation is now attached to the original document, so this is now in evidence without marking it for identification. Mr. Tolimir, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Could we now pull up in e-court 65 ter document P16?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not sure that the number is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, can you please repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Could we see 65 ter 16, 1-6. Thank you. This is the document that we wanted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Please take a look at the document. It says that the subject is: "Request for Mobilisation of Buses for Transportation of Personnel." Who was it signed by, do you recognise the signature? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is signed by Assistant Minister of Defence Momcilo Kovacevic, and this is indeed his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell from this signature where this document came from, which organ?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, judging by the signature and by the function, I can conclude that this is a document from the Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Is the letterhead missing? Should it appear above the date and the number? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the letterhead is missing. The Ministry of Defence letterhead.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document, 65 ter 16. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This relates also to the subject: "Request for Mobilisation of Buses for Transportation of Personnel." It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the 65 ter document 16 shall be assigned Exhibit D347. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now see in e-court 1D13038. Thank you. I will repeat: 1D1038. I'm sorry, I omitted the 0. Thank you to Aleksandar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We see that this is a document from the Ministry of Defence, the Secretariat of the Ministry of Defence in Zvornik, and it is addressed to the Pale Ministry of Defence, and the subject is: "Report on Mobilisation of Vehicles." My question: Can you tell us what this document is about and why it is that the Zvornik Ministry of Defence is sending this communication, this document, to the Ministry of Defence, Pale? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Secretariat of the Ministry of Defence in Zvornik had the obligation - and we saw this in the order that you showed me earlier - to report the Ministry of Defence on what they had done in order to mobilise these vehicles, and this is, indeed, that report, from which we can see exactly the number of buses that have been mobilised. If you would like me to read it, I can do so. But this is a report sent to the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Again, we do have an English on Sanction, and I see some important information on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this assistance to the Defence. It says, inter alia: "We wish to inform you that we have mobilised and sent the following by 2200 hours on the 12th of July, 1995: "6 articulated buses; "34 50-seater buses; "2 minibuses; "21 lorries and articulated lorries." And then it continues: "Further mobilisation is not possible as all possibilities have been exhausted and passenger transport has been paralysed." Mr. Tolimir, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, can you tell us: Was this telegram acted upon by the addressee and did they report to their ministry what their capabilities were and what they did in order to implement the order? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what they said, that all the possibilities were exhausted.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Is it possible to attach the translation to the original document in the same procedure as with did it with the last document?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 1D1038 shall be assigned Exhibit D348. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. And thank you to the secretary -- to the Registrar. Could we now see P2121, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: 2521, interpreter correction.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: This is a document from the Drina Corps command, dated the 12th of July, 1995, sent as a very urgent document to the Main Staff, the command post and rear command post for information. I will read the relevant part: "Pursuant to the Main Staff of the VRS commander's order to provide 50 buses for evacuation from the Srebrenica enclave, we hereby ask you for additional approval of the following types and quantities of fuel. "Diesel fuel: 10.000 litres. "Petrol: 2.000 litres. "On 12 July 1995 and onward, buses will be used from the municipalities of Pale, Sokolac, Visegrad, Rogatica, Han Pijesak, Milici, Sekovici, Bratunac, and Zvornik. The final destination is unknown at the moment. A representative of the Drina Corps shall take delivery of the quantities approved immediately upon your approval." And it is signed by the commander Major General Milenko Zivanovic. As we can see the stamp is quite legible here, so can you tell us what these abbreviations mean that I read. Unfortunately, I did not quote them. It says "PK" and "PKM." It says "KM" and "PKM." Sent to the Main Staff, and then "KM" and "PKM." Thank you. And what is this "for information" a reference to?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: KM stands for "command post." And it's the command post of the Main Staff of the VRS. The PKM abbreviation stands for "rear command post." You also asked about the reference to "for information."

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: That's right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For this quantity of fuel, the only authorised person to approve them is the commander of the Main Staff of the VRS, and now since this is something that falls within the purview of logistics, they are informed of this information. This is for their information so that they can expect that this amount of fuel will be requisitioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell me whether the Ministry of Defence has anything to do with this, and the minister, and whether he issued any orders to that effect? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if I understood you correctly. Did you ask about whether my sector had anything to do with this? Well, the sector where I worked had nothing to do with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. The instance that sent this telegram, this organ, did they -- did they actually take over the subject matter from some decision made by someone else, and if so, whose decision?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command of the Drina Corps, or, rather, its commander, Major Milenko Zivanovic, makes a reference here to the order of the Main Staff of the VRS on the provision of 50 vehicles that will need fuel.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. So my question then is this: Does this mean that the corps commander received the document approving the use of the quantities of fuel mentioned here? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, as I sit here I can't really -- and based on this, I cannot conclude whether he received a document or an oral order, but in any case it would have had to come from the commander of the Main Staff of the VRS, which is clear from this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, please tell us, based on all these documents that I showed you, did the VRS inform the Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska of the purpose of these vehicles, what they were went to be used for? The vehicles that were mobilised. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they only received -- they were only informed that they should mobilise the buses and where they should mobilise them from and where they should send them to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the telegram that we saw earlier, the outgoing telegram, your telegram, did you mention in that telegram -- did you make any reference to any additional requests in terms of the time-frame or the needs of the buses?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't add remarks of any kind to that document. If the term "evacuation" was used, well, it's a general term and you wouldn't know what needs to be evacuated. Buses are, in general, used to evacuate people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me, if the general is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. If the general is, as I believe, and I think the witness believes, is asking General Skrbic about his particular document, could we see that up on the screen? Because he's referring to specific things in it, and I think it would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Indeed, I would appreciate that. Can you provide the Registry with a document number?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you, Mr. McCloskey. Let's now see P2520. Thank you. And then Mr. McCloskey will be able to see what he is interested in. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And in relation to this document, Mr. Skrbic, you were asked by Mr. Tolimir: "Did you make any reference to any additional requests in terms of the time-frame or the needs of the buses?"

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. McCloskey, for giving me the opportunity to have a look at the document. I don't have to rely on my memory. I didn't send any additional requests to the Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska. And here we have seen what the document says, quite clearly, so it's not necessary to repeat these things now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The -- but the question was --

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- if you have added to the request for the buses anything which could indicate the purpose of this request.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I apologise to Mr. Skrbic. Perhaps I wasn't precise. This matter might be clarified. Is this the only request that you submitted to the Ministry of Defence in relation to this issue? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I can't remember exactly how many such requests there were, but I quite clearly remember that we submitted a similar request for the mobilisation of buses in the Banja Luka area towards the end of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Could you please tell us which organisational units of the VRS Main Staff are located in Han Pijesak? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the question concerns the wartime period, from 1992 to 1995. During that period of time in Han Pijesak at the rear command post, there was the logistics sector, the sector for mobilisation and personnel affairs, and the editorial board of the Republika Srpska paper. Towards the end of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the year correctly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- the sector for morale guidance and legal affairs was also transferred there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Wait a moment, please, Mr. Tolimir. Can you repeat the year? The interpreters didn't catch it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From 1992 to 1995 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: From 1992 to 1996, said the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, please tell us, at the time of the event in Srebrenica, were you involved in any extraordinary activities at the rear command post? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the 18th of July, 1995, we had only organised defence for the rear command post, direct and indirect defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. From whom did you receive an order according to which you should only organise direct and indirect defence, as you said, in order to defend, protect, the rear command post? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We received an order from the commander of the VRS Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you remember the reason for which it was necessary to take the protective measures that you organised at the rear command post? What was the reason for taking these measures?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was necessary to take measures because of the information according to which armed forces were breaking through the forest, via the roads through Han Pijesak, and information according to which they were in the immediate vicinity of the rear command post. And as a result of this information, we, ourselves, had to organise our defence because the 65th Protection Regiment that had such a responsibility did not have enough units to make it possible for it to protect that rear command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us where this attack on the rear command post was launched from and by which enemy forces, if you have any such information? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The forces that broke through these roads from Srebrenica and Zepa in the direction of Olovo and Kladanj, these forces had to pass through the forest through Romanija and Han Pijesak itself. And for a stretch of the road, they had to pass through the area above Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could we just double-check that we have the date correct, that this happened after July 18th? Or is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, can you please clarify that with the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I asked the witness which additional activities were taken at the rear command post at the time of the events in Srebrenica, and he answered as he did. I don't understand what additional questions I should put to him, but I'll put other questions to him. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But in that case I will ask the witness: When did that take place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we received the order to organise the defence on the 18th of July, 1995. That is when we received that order to organise this defence ourselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And after that day you carried out this order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, please carry on. Just a moment, Judge Nyambe has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you. I have a clarification for the witness. At page 23, line 10 of today's transcript, the question from General Tolimir was: "Could you tell us where this attack on the rear command post was launched from and by which enemy forces?" Your answer doesn't seem to answer the second question which refers to "by which enemy forces." Could you please answer that question? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe I was more precise. An attack wasn't launched but a breakthrough of Muslim armed forces from Srebrenica and Zepa was expected, and it was expected that they would come down the roads from Srebrenica and Zepa, the roads that went to Olovo and Kladanj and Tuzla, and the roads that pass through the location where the rear command post is located, which is in Han Pijesak. And there was, in fact, an armed conflict, but one wouldn't define that or characterise that as an attack. They were breaking through, Your Honours. They didn't have an organised attack. They hadn't organised an attack of any kind. They were just breaking through, and if they ran into our forces, then they would open fire and there would be a conflict. Both sides would open fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can you help me to clarify it, finally. Which enemy forces are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the members of the 28th Muslim Division of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina that was in Herzegovina, and I think there was the 324th or some other brigade from the ABiH, from Zepa. The name is not that important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, where were the forces of the 65th Protection Motorised Regiment that were supposed to defend the rear command post? Could you tell us where they were?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I don't know where they were, but they weren't in Crna Rijeka nor were they in Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know whether on the 18th of July any action was taken from Zepa in the direction of the Main Staff and its units, and was any action taken by units from the Main Staff, for example, the Protection Regiment? Was any activity undertaken in the direction of Zepa, for example? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm only aware of an armed conflict at the village of Mokro, on the road from Han Pijesak towards Sokolac. As for what happened in Crna Rijeka, I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us about what you know. Where was action taken along the road we have been referring to?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The members of the Muslim forces broke through via that road. About 5.00 in the morning they came across our defence forces. It was dawning. When they saw them, they opened fire. And naturally, the members of the Army of Republika Srpska responded. Two of their members were then killed. When I say "two of their members," I'm referring to members of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, to these Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know whether any buses were mobilised for the evacuation of the inhabitants in Zepa when they were evacuating to the territory under the control of the ABiH? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Was this done in an identical manner, as was the case for the evacuation of the population of Srebrenica? Or could you tell us in what manner this evacuation was carried out? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That question assumes that the -- the general has told us about the evacuation of people from Srebrenica and he hasn't said that yet. We've got into buses to go to Bratunac, but he can't answer that question without the foundation of it being brought out first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is a formulation matter, I would agree. On the other hand, this witness is capable to answer this question even in this way, I suppose. Do you intend to rephrase your question or would you repeat it, Mr. Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I'll repeat my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, do you know whether buses were mobilised to evacuate the civilian population from Zepa?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know about that. But it's a matter of mobilising buses, and they were mobilised in the same way as the buses for Srebrenica. Nothing else is at stake, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. There was an interpretation mistake because in my first question I also asked the witness about the mobilisation of buses. My question is as follows: Did Tolimir or anyone else play a role during the mobilisation of buses, or was it only the organs responsible for mobilisation that had a role to play in that? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hope that from the answers given thus far we all realise that the mobilisation of buses was in the hands of the sector in which I worked. General Tolimir had nothing to do with the mobilisation of buses, and neither did his sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have in e-court Exhibit P2656. Thank you. Thank you, but that's not the one. Can we have the document that we saw a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can you give us the correct number? Are you asking for P2521?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We see the Prosecution document on our screens. That's the one that I requested.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, let us take a look at paragraph 2 under the number which begins with the name "Krsmanovic," colon, and then it says "Toso."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: For the sake of the record, I would like to know the document number of this document. Mr. Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is document Exhibit P2656. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I quote what it says in this telegram. "Krsmanovic in a discussion about the problem of transportation made reference to 10 buses ... or trucks in relation to the means that are not mobilised. 'That was the situation today.'" So he's talking about to someone whose name is Toso. Now this is my question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, you said that this is a telegram. I have some doubt if this is a telegram. Can you please introduce this document in a way that the witness is aware of the character of this specific document? What is it about?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. This is a transcript produced by the Muslims -- actually, a transcript of an allegedly intercepted conversation which took place at 11.00 on the 16th of July, 1995. If you look at the back page, you can see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I see a time indication of 2143 hours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this note be reversed so that the witness can see the exact time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What do you mean by that? Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is only one page of the document admitted through one of the previous witnesses. I think this was a confidential document, and I think that at that time we mentioned the date of the 16th of July, and this is how it's been recorded in the e-court. Therefore, I don't think that the Prosecution have any problem with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, and I was merely going to state that it would help the witness to have the date, and I -- and General Tolimir did that, and I agree that, um, as you recall how the dates are sorted out it is -- I agree that 16 July is the -- is the date that's in the record in this -- regarding this intercept.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Is this document under seal? It's not. Okay, please now put your question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, based on the contents of this document -- of this intercept, are you able to discern who Krsmanovic is and who Toso is and whereabouts they were located?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that this is a notebook with some handwritten entries, and as Mr. Tolimir said, it relates to a conversation between a Krsmanovic and a Toso. I knew two men by the name of Krsmanovic. One was from the Ministry of Defence and the other was the chief of staff of the 2nd Romanija Brigade of the VRS. Now, I knew a lot of Tolimir's and Todovic's people from the Drina Corps, the Banja Luka Corps, and so on and so forth, and it is possible that this nickname, Toso, could have referred to any one of them. Now, hypothetically speaking, if Mr. Krsmanovic from the Ministry of Defence talked to someone, that means that he had even more possibilities to talk with a person named Toso in Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Who is Toso?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we are talking about the Main Staff, "Toso" would mean Zdravko Tolimir. And then in the Republika Srpska and in the Republic of Serbia, Your Honour, there are millions of people called Toso which is a derivative from their last name Todovic or Todorovic or whatever. Well, I remember just now, in the security detail of Manojlo Milovanovic there was a non-commissioned officer with the last name of Todic and we also used to call him "Toso." But in view of the context of this intercept, I don't think he was the collocutor of Mr. Krsmanovic. I don't think he has anything to do with this. Also, the president of the supreme military court of Republika Srpska was a man called Novak Todorovic, and we used to call him Toso as well, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir, we are now at 10.30. I think it is time for our first break. We will resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, can you please tell us whether the participants in this radio communication, this Krsmanovic and Toso, did they have to be within the same network in order to carry out this conversation?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. However, if they had been in different radio network, was that a situation that would impose for those listening in to register the relay between them?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that would be the proper procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Now, back to this Krsmanovic person whom you knew from the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps and the other one. Was he in the same network with the Main Staff where Toso, Tolimir, was, and was the Drina Corps where General Tolimir, also known as Toso, could have been?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tolimir, for reminding me of Aleksa Krsmanovic who was assistant commander of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps for logistics. He was the one that elapsed [as interpreted] my memory. Had he been one of the collocutors, they would have been in the same network.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, those conversing within the same radio network, people from the Ministry of Defence and the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, did they have to establish a connection with the Main Staff through relay devices or could they have done it directly?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The communication that you are talking about could not have been established without a relay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I was referring to a radio relay mediator or go-between. Radio relay is a device or a switching board, and that's what Mr. Gajic reminded me of. Now, back to my question, did you have that in mind when you gave me your answer?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The communication lines within the army were carried out via the same radio relay, without any mediating devices. Other communications had to go through some go-betweens for the purpose of clearances.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, can you please try and speak a little bit more slowly, and I'll do the same, because this is causing problems for the interpreters. Can you please now look at the contents of the conversation between Krsmanovic and Toso. Can you tell me whether those who were intercepting this conversation recorded any words uttered by Toso in the course of this conversation?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here "Krsmanovic," and then colon. And then we have the text which says: "Toso, concerning the problems of transportation mentioned in a discussion 10 buses ... and trucks in relation to the means ... 'and that was the case today.'" Apparently there is no response coming from Toso.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us, please, as a soldier, was this a verbatim record of the conversation or is it just a summary of the intercept between these two persons?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apparently this is a summary.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. We are now going to move to a different topic, but it also pertains to July 1995.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Tolimir please repeat the second part of his question. It was inaudible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, the interpreters had a problem with the second part of your question. Could you repeat it, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I said: Mr. Skrbic, we are now going to move to another topic concerning July 1995. We are going to talk about retirements that affected your sector as well. My question is as follows: Who was authorised to sign retirement documents for the officers of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, there are different levels of authority when it comes to retirement of VRS officers. I wouldn't like to tire you with lengthy explanations going from NCO up to the rank of general. I'd like just to tell you what was within the responsibility of the Main Staff of the VRS. Up to the lieutenant-colonel rank, the commander of the Main Staff, General Mladic, was the authorised person. All the officers with the colonel rank are retired and promoted by the minister of defence of Republika Srpska. As for generals, they are retired or promoted by Mr. Karadzic who was, at the time, the president of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic, for this answer. Do you remember that in mid-July 1995, if anyone from the VRS was pensioned off?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, your question is very broad. I can only remember the generals who were retired then. As for other officers - and there were others who were retired, too - I can't really recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. Can you remember any general who was retired in mid-July 1995?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was General Milenko Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember when he retired and who was responsible for the paperwork for his retirement?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The decree that I took to the president of the republic was signed by the president of the republic, Dr. Radovan Karadzic, on the 14th of July, 1995. The decree defined specifically the date of the retirement, and I believe that was on that same day; in other words, as of July 14th, 1995, he was retired.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, on the 14th of July, 1995, in formal or casual conversations with Dr. Karadzic when you took this decree for his signing it, did you touch upon the topic of Srebrenica in any way? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not talk at all about anything. Now, Your Honour, may I put a question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Sorry, no, this is not possible. You are the witness and you are here to answer questions. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did you attend the send-off ceremony for General Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to apologise for what I've asked earlier, because I would just like to point out a matter that is relevant, and I don't know what the procedure is going to be here because I am supposed to testify in the Karadzic case as well. That was the only question that I wanted to put. I had no other questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You were, as you told us, at the beginning of your testimony, already a witness in two other cases. This is a normal procedure and you have to provide us with your full knowledge about things you are asked here in the courtroom. Perhaps you are asked similar questions in the Karadzic trial, that may happen, but nevertheless you are obliged to answer these questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I would like to thank Mr. Skrbic as well. Mr. Skrbic, did you attend the send-off ceremony that was organised on the occasion of General Zivanovic's retirement, and if so, where was that?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The send-off ceremony was on -- at a restaurant on the way from Han Pijesak to Sokolac on --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the date.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- 1995, and I attended personally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the name of the restaurant and the date when this took place.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was the Jela restaurant, and the date is the 20th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And I would like to thank Mr. Skrbic as well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now can we move on to another matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before you move on to another matter, I would like to put a question to the witness in relation to this topic. You said you took the papers about the retirement of General Zivanovic to the president of the Republika Srpska. You -- that means in your sector these documents were prepared, if I am not mistaken. Who ordered you to do all this work and to bring the documents to the president?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I received the order from the commander of the Main Staff, General Mladic, to prepare the paperwork and to take them to the president of the republic for his signature. Otherwise, I could not do it without the commander's orders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And you handed these documents over to the president himself, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I was in the office of the president waiting for him to sign the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Did you meet him personally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Judge Mindua.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Skrbic, a question regarding the promotions and the retirement. You said that for ranks that are inferior to the rank of colonel, it was the minister of defence that was deciding for them; but we see that when it comes to a general, it's General Mladic who was taking the initiative. He would ask you to bring the documents to the president of the republic for him to sign them. Now, when it comes to majors and lieutenant-generals, who would take the initiative to prepare the documents and to bring them to the minister for his signing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, no documents or paperwork was prepared at the Ministry of Defence. Everything was prepared at the sector at the Main Staff where I worked, both the orders and the decrees. The orders for promotions and retirement -- for promotions and retirement at the level of colonel, we would forward to or take personally to the minister of defence; whereas for generals, we would take them to the president of the republic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not really understand your answer, and also the transcript is not completely clear. On page 37, line 21 and 22, we see that it says about majors and lieutenant-generals, but I wanted to know what happens when it came to the promotion and retirement of ranks that are inferior to the ranks of colonel, lieutenant-colonel, major, captain, who was drafting those documents so that the minister of defence can sign them? That is my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All the paperwork was prepared at the sector for mobilisation, organisation, and personnel matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For generals and also for ranks that are inferior to the rank of colonel; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For ranks below the rank of colonel, we did not send them to the Ministry of Defence. From the level of major to lieutenant-colonel, all the documents were signed by the commander of the Main Staff of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: To clarify this matter, I take it that there is a distinction -- or you made a distinction between "paperwork" and "signature." All paperwork was done in your sector you were the head of as assistant commander, and the signature, the formal decision was sometimes made at a higher [Realtime transcript read in error "later"] level in the Ministry of Defence or by the president of the republic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exactly so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Tolimir, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. And thank you, Judge Mindua.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Skrbic, please tell us, was the procedure -- was the standard procedure, as it says here, that all documents on retirements and promotions of generals should be -- are to be taken personally by the chief of the sector for mobilisation, organisation, and personnel to the Supreme Commander? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what was ordered by General Mladic. Otherwise, he would have had to go and take those documents and that paperwork himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I would like to put a correction of the transcript on the record. Page 38, line 25, I didn't say "made at a later level" but "at a higher level." Now carry on, please, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Skrbic, can you tell us, please, why is it necessary for either the commander or chief of sector, the sector for organisation, mobilisation, and personnel, why was it necessary for them to go to the Supreme Commander in the cases where retirement or promotions of generals were concerned? Why was that necessary?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because -- my apologies. Because the -- it was within the exclusive purview of the president of the republic, as the Supreme Commander, to issue all documents that related to generals.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, at the farewell reception for General Zivanovic, was there any discussion, did anyone talk about the events in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, there was no mention of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. Since you were involved in mobilisation issues at the Main Staff, can you tell us what exactly the term "general mobilisation" implies? What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The term "general mobilisation" implies that this is a process that has to be announced via the public media. It is no longer confidential. And this information is to be used by all elements, all subjects within the Republika Srpska, including the military, so that they can focus on mobilisation both of personnel and materiel. And all subjects within the republic are duty-bound via the Ministry of Defence to mobilise whatever it is that is required of them. In general mobilisation, the army does not have to demand that its units be fully staffed because that would depend on the situation on the front lines or at the theater of war. Rather, the personnel levels would be filled depending on the needs. When it was -- when the requirements were greater, then the mobilisation would include a larger segment of the population. But when general mobilisation is declared, the state thereby, in fact, informs or let it be known by everyone in the republic that people have to respond to the call-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, from your personal experience, do you know whether the same principle for general mobilisation was in force in the territories of other republics of the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I am aware of that based on the various analysis that our department prepared within the Army of Yugoslavia. The president of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Alija Izetbegovic, declared general mobilisation on the 4th of April, 1992. Or, in fact, at the time, the JNA was still in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, could you tell us -- could you tell the Trial Chamber -- or could you draw a parallel between that and when general mobilisation was declared in Republika Srpska? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, it was similarly done in Republika Srpska. The difference, however, was in that the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina immediately declared a state of war or imminent threat of war covering the entire territory under their control; whereas the Republika Srpska did not declare a state of war until 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us what's the difference between proclaiming a state of war and an imminent threat of war and mobilisation and proclaiming an imminent threat of war? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mobilisation is a process that is included in the idea of an imminent threat of war and a state of war. An immediate threat of war is a concept that covers processes and actions that involve preparing all segments of society for war. A state of war is the most serious category in any state, since in such a situation, production, the economy, and everything else is focussed on supplying the armed forces. Not just the army, but the armed forces as a whole. And the armed forces in Republika Srpska were -- consisted of the VRS and the units and members of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. "General mobilisation," what does that term mean? Could you please tell us what kinds of general mobilisation, in fact, exist? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is an open mobilisation and a secret mobilisation. Public and secret.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Could you please tell me what the difference is, since I interrupted you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The difference is that secret general mobilisation is not something that is made public over the media; but public mobilisation is something that is made known over the media so that the entire population of Republika Srpska, of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina could be warned -- or, rather, informed about their obligations.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skrbic. Could you please tell us, can you proclaim mobilisation in only one part of the territory of a given republic or state? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, if that's what you had in mind, yes. You can proclaim mobilisation in a segment of one's territory. You can proclaim mobilisation and a state of war in a segment of the territory, but when you proclaim such a state in part of the territory, then it's not general mobilisation. General mobilisation concerns a state as a whole. Since I know that this was the case, a state of war was proclaimed in a segment of the territory before a state of war was proclaimed for the entire republic. That was the case in the zone of responsibility of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, and then that was also the case in the zone of responsibility of the 2nd Krajina Corps, which is in the western part near Drvar. And a state of war was also proclaimed in the area of responsibility of the Drina Corps. I think that that state of war was proclaimed after Srebrenica. Throughout the territory of Republika Srpska a state of war was proclaimed in October 1995 and not earlier than October. I think that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see the following document on the screen, 1D962. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. We can see a document from the communication centre of the Main Staff. It's the encryption department in Sarajevo. It's dated the 14th of July, 1995, and at the bottom it says, "Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina," the War Presidency, and the date, the 14th of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think it would be useful to see the English translation of the document 1D269. 1D269. It's document D120 that was marked for identification; however, since D109 was a reproduction in something that was published, this is a document disclosed to us by the Prosecution. It's a better copy, a far better copy, but the translation of these two documents is the same. And we now have it up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And can you give us the correct number of this document we have on the screen? There were so many numbers mentioned. Which is the document number we have on the screen in front of us?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The number, the original document's number, to the left, is 1D962. And to the right, there is just the translation of that very same document but that document isn't a copy of the original. It's a copy from a book. In the meantime we found the original document that was disclosed to us by the Prosecution, and this document has now also been uploaded and this document's number is 1D962, and that's the document we will be using now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to thank Aleksandar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I was told that we have two versions of the same document. One is in front of us, this is 1D962, with the English translation. The document D102 was previously marked for identification with another witness was unable to identify this document. So it would be helpful if the translation would be attached to both versions, and we can decide later. If you are tendering this version we have now on the screen, then we could probably receive it and vacate the other one. That would be one way of action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, I correct myself. The previous one would then just remain marked for identification because it was used. Okay. Mr. Tolimir, please carry on and put questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I will read out part of the document before I put my question to you. This document was sent from Zepa to the presidency of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and it says: "The following was adopted at the War Presidency of Zepa municipality, held on 14th of July, 1995: "I. General mobilisation is hereby proclaimed on the territory of Zepa municipality. "II. All available resources will be used for defence purposes. "III. All citizens fit for work will be put at the disposal of the Zepa municipality civilian protection staff. "IV. All persons who are fit for military service and are currently under work obligation will be placed at the disposal of the 5th Eastern Bosnia Light Brigade, except for the members of the Zepa War Presidency who will be in permanent session and other employees who, at the decision of the Zepa Municipal War Presidency, will remain at the disposal of the Zepa Municipal War Presidency. "V. Members of the Zepa Public Security Station will act in accordance with the orders in the defence of the free territory of the municipality of Zepa. "VI. Members of the population who have firearms in their possession are hereby ordered to place them at the disposal of the brigade, otherwise they will be prosecuted. "VII. This decision shall come into effect immediately." It was signed by the president of the War Presidency of Zepa municipality, Mehmed Hajric, and you can see the five addresses that it was sent to. My question is as follows: Could you tell us whether this is a typical general document on general mobilisation in part of a given territory? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tolimir. And this is under conditions when a state of war was proclaimed because this individual signed in his capacity as the president of the War Presidency, which is possible only if a state of war prevails.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Skrbic, please, could you tell us what it means when it says that all resources available should be placed at their disposal? And that's what it says under item II.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was probably already done, but this subject is informing the presidency of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina that it shall place all resources at the disposal of the army; that is to say, the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to know what "all resources" actually means? What does "all resources" mean?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "All resources" means weapons, artillery, food, everything that they had. Everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that also include all men fit for the military?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. If you, on this date mentioned here, the 14th of July, obtained information about such a decision, what would such information mean for you as a general from the other side? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a very revealing document from which one could draw the conclusion that a large-scale offensive might be launched.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. If such a document is issued then concerning part of the territory that was supposed to be demilitarised, what does this mean for those who attributed the status of a demilitarised zone to the area in question?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SKRBIC [Resumed]
